reply: We need to know what you are measuring – the API identity or its concentration – and the melt’s optical properties. Once those are clear we can pick a probe that survives the hot, fouling environment and gives a usable signal.

report.title: Hot Polymer Extrusion – Initial Probe Selection

stated: developing hot polymer extrusion process with active pharmaceutical ingredient
want to investigate if optical measurement can detect composition changes while melt is processed
have offline assays but process interface is hot and may be exposed to material build up
need initial comparison plan and questions required before choosing a probe
unknowns: temperature and pressure at probe location
available port size and access points

questions.text: What is the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and its expected concentration range in the polymer melt?
What is the approximate optical density (OD) or scattering level of the melt at the measurement wavelength range?
What are the temperature and pressure conditions at the intended probe location?
What is the size and type of the available port or interface for probe installation?
Do you have any constraints on probe material (e.g., must withstand high temperature and chemical exposure)?
